headline: High-risk default interaction: shared Replit workspace plus ACI’s broad egress can leak or corrupt CRM/email data when paired with Replit Agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can ingest and emit content through MCP/direct function calls, while Replit Agent can read and write Repl workspace files. That creates a plausible shared-channel injection path if ACI writes attacker-controlled text into files that Replit Agent later treats as instructions. The pathway is not proven by docs, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ACI writes untrusted content into a Repl workspace file that Replit Agent later parses as instructions
IF Replit Agent is configured to follow file contents as task directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep ACI outputs in a dedicated data file format, not task prompts
Add a manual review step before Replit Agent consumes ACI-generated files
Prefix all ACI-generated artifacts with non-executable metadata headers
requires-engineering: enforce provenance tags on files passed between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches CRM, email, calendar, and customer support data and has broad network egress; Replit Agent can read filesystem contents and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive records can move from ACI into Replit Agent’s context and then out to third-party services. The pair’s default surfaces make leakage plausible without special setup.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same Repl workspace or copied files containing CRM/email data
IF Replit Agent forwards those files or summaries to external APIs or deployments
mitigations: Separate sensitive ACI data from the Replit workspace
Redact CRM/email fields before any handoff
Disable outbound calls for the Replit task until review
Use a throwaway workspace for non-sensitive test data
requires-engineering: add DLP filters on file handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ACI supports multiple instances and broad API-driven actions, while Replit Agent can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a persistent Repl. If both touch the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes can overwrite code, secrets, or deployment config. The overlap is dangerous by default because neither profile shows locking or coordination.
conditions: IF ACI and Replit Agent modify the same repository or workspace concurrently
IF git state or deployment files are edited without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or directory
Pause one agent while the other writes
Require manual git review before commits
Store secrets outside the shared workspace
requires-engineering: add file-level locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM/email/calendar actions and Replit Agent can act on files and deployments, so ACI output may become operational input for Replit Agent. Without a documented verification step, errors or hallucinations from ACI can cascade into code, deployment, or customer-facing actions. The blast radius is meaningful but not automatically irreversible in every case.
conditions: IF Replit Agent consumes ACI-produced text, tickets, or configs as authoritative input
IF no human or automated verification step checks ACI outputs before action
mitigations: Require a second-pass review of ACI outputs
Use structured schemas instead of free-form text
Log source provenance on every handoff
Block deployment actions until approval
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles CRM, email, and customer support data, while Replit Agent handles secrets and deployment configuration in a cloud Repl. If regulated or customer data is copied into the Replit workspace, retention and residency obligations can diverge across the two services. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF customer data or secrets from ACI are stored in the Replit workspace
IF the two services have different retention, residency, or deletion handling for that data class
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the Replit workspace
Minimize retention by deleting copied artifacts after use
Use synthetic data for development tasks
Review vendor data-processing terms before sharing records
requires-engineering: implement policy-based data routing
